title: Ad-hoc Tenant Snapshot Export: Audit-ready One-click Onboarding & Delivery
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create an audit-ready, one-click tenant snapshot export flow in the Console that lets enterprise customers generate and deliver time-bound usage + cost + config snapshots for compliance reviews and audits. The feature should support templated exports, encrypted delivery (S3/SFTP), RBAC gating, and clear cost estimates before export. Goal is to reduce manual support exports and accelerate SOC/finance audits.
acceptance_criteria: Console UI: 'Create Snapshot Export' wizard available under Tenant > Exports with stepper for scope, format, delivery, and confirmation
Export scope options: usage (token counts), per-route cost breakdowns, model version tags, dedicated capacity metadata, and recent console ACLs/audit logs
Delivery targets: S3 (customer bucket), SFTP endpoint, or direct download (zipped, encrypted). For S3/SFTP, store encrypted manifest and provide verification checksum
Pre-export estimate: show token volume estimate and approximate outbound egress charges and expected processing time
RBAC: only users with 'Export:tenant-snapshot' permission may create exports; export events logged to audit trail with job ID
API parity: Admin API endpoint for programmatic snapshot creation matching Console flow
Retention and TTL: exports auto-expire from Customer S3 staging after configurable TTL; download links are one-time and short-lived
Telemetry: job lifecycle metrics (queued, processing, completed, failed) surfaced in Console and telemetry pipeline for SLOs
Security: keys encrypted with KMS, SFTP credentials stored in Secrets Manager, and security review completed before GA
design_notes: Proposed UX: default to 'Scoped Snapshot' with templates (Compliance, Finance, Ops) to reduce configuration errors
Edge case: large tenants (>100M tokens/day) should be warned and recommended to run via API or scheduled off-peak window
engineering_notes: Backend: leverage existing export runner (PM-33478) but add streaming multipart archive support to avoid memory spikes
Compute: use dedicated export workers with batching/kv-cache bypass to avoid impacting realtime inference lanes
Data contracts: export schema v1 with explicit version in manifest and example JSON in Confluence (link below)
Cost: estimate CPU/GPU work for large exports and add throttling; provide cost chargeback labels in job metadata
risks_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: implementing in-console increases surface area for support but accelerates self-serve; alternative is API-only initial launch
Risk: generating large archives may stress storage pipelines—mitigated by streaming + TTL + chunked upload
Compliance: storing exported PII requires opt-in and stronger KMS policies; default templates should redact PII where possible
